# Research question

**Research question:**

Among adults aged 60 to 75 in primary care diagnosed with COPD, does **smoking status** have any association with how far they are able walk within 6 minutes measured at baseline and six times more over 6 months, taking into account their usual **level of physical activity**?

> It would be beneficial to understand whether there is a pattern in how far the participants are able to walk within 6 minutes during each follow up depending on their smoking status and whether their usual **level of physical activity** also affects the distance they are able to walk. If there is, then a further analysis into how much it affects and whether a baseline for each permutation exists by finding their means and standard deviation (or median and IQR), followed up with knowing if a progression or even regression exists at each follow-up. It is worth knowing the relationships between these exposures as it could serve as a promoting point for avoiding smoking as well as having a better physical activity level despite having COPD. An initial assumption around this research question is that active smokers should have a lower distance walked in 6 minutes while participants with higher level of physical activity should have higher distance walked. However, the following analyses will prove or disprove this hypothesis.

# Data import and structure

```{r import}
# Baseline data
baseline = read.table('data/Baseline_Data.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t')
str(baseline)
summary(baseline)

# Visits data
visits = read.table('data/Visits_Data.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t')
str(visits)
summary(visits)
visits_per_id = aggregate(visit ~ ID, data = visits, FUN = length)
unique(visits_per_id$visit)
nrow(visits_per_id[visits_per_id$visit == 7, ])
nrow(visits_per_id[visits_per_id$visit == 6, ])
```

The baseline data contains 501 rows of data with 10 columns (variables). Some of the data types from the baseline data are not automatically the correct data type according to the dictionary and also contain some NA values. Possible duplicate ID shown from the baseline summary with 501 observations but only 500 unique values. The visits data contains 3466 rows of data with 3 columns (variables), each participants are expected to have 7 visits total but 20 participants only have 6 visits while 478 participants have the full 7 visits.

# Data quality assessment and cleaning

## Baseline data

```{r clean-baseline}
# Duplicates
baseline[duplicated(baseline$ID), 'ID']
baseline[baseline$ID == 'COPD000078', ] # Exact same row, index 78 and 501

# Factor columns: sex, smoker, phy_activity, diabetes, ethnicity, inhaler
# Sex
unique(baseline$sex)
baseline[baseline$sex == 12, ] # 1 row

# Smoker
unique(baseline$smoker)
baseline[baseline$smoker == -999, ] # 3 rows

# phy_activity
unique(baseline$phy_activity)
baseline[baseline$phy_activity == 'Hihg' &
    !is.na(baseline$phy_activity), ] # 6 rows; Typo 'Hihg'

# Diabetes
unique(baseline$diabetes) # No issues

# Ethnicity
unique(baseline$ethnicity)
baseline[baseline$ethnicity == 4 &
    !is.na(baseline$ethnicity), -1] # 4 rows; Unclear error

# Inhaler
unique(baseline$inhaler) # No issues

# Numerical / continuous columns: age, bmi
numerical_baseline_cols = c('age', 'bmi')
summary(baseline[, numerical_baseline_cols])

# BMI
head(baseline[order(baseline$bmi, decreasing = TRUE),
    c('ID', 'bmi')]) # Irregular BMI values of 288.0, 295.0

# Exacerbations
unique(baseline$exacerbations) # No issues

# Handling data issues
baseline = baseline[-501, ] # Duplicate
baseline$sex[baseline$sex == 12] = NA  # Sex
baseline$smoker[baseline$smoker == -999] = NA # Smoker
baseline$phy_activity[baseline$phy_activity == 'Hihg'] = 'High' # Physical activity
baseline$ethnicity[baseline$ethnicity == 4] = NA  # Ethnicity
baseline$bmi[baseline$bmi == 288 | baseline$bmi == 295] = NA # BMI

# Factor type of each categorical variables as new variables
baseline$fsex = factor(baseline$sex, levels = c(1, 2),
    labels = c('Female', 'Male')
)
baseline$fsmoker = factor(baseline$smoker, levels = c(0, 1, 2),
    labels = c('Never smoked', 'Ex smoker', 'Current smoker')
)
baseline$fphy_activity = factor(baseline$phy_activity,
    labels = c('Low', 'Moderate', 'High', 'Very_high')
)
baseline$fdiabetes = factor(baseline$diabetes, levels = c(0, 1),
    labels = c('No', 'Yes')
)
baseline$fethnicity = factor(baseline$ethnicity, levels = c(1, 2, 3),
    labels = c('Group1', 'Group2', 'Group3')
)
baseline$finhaler = factor(baseline$inhaler, levels = c(0, 1),
    labels = c('Not receiving inhaler', 'Receiving inhaler')
)
```

# Missing data

## Baseline data

```{r missing-baseline, include = FALSE}
# Baseline
colSums(is.na(baseline))

# Smoker
baseline[is.na(baseline$smoker), -1] # No clear pattern

# Physical activity
baseline[is.na(baseline$phy_activity), -1] # No clear pattern

# Diabetes
baseline[is.na(baseline$diabetes), -1] # No clear pattern

# Ethnicity
baseline[is.na(baseline$ethnicity), -1] # No clear pattern
```

Missing data in the baseline data occured in the variables: **smoking status, usual level of physical activity, diabetes status, and ethnicity** with not very clear patterns on the missingness

| Variable | Total missing | Pattern | Type of missing |
|:-----------------|:-----------------|:-----------------|:-----------------|
| Smoking status | 3 rows | Too little data to find any missing patterns | Missing completely at random |
| Usual level of physical activity | 14 rows | Majority of the missing occurred are participants receiving inhaler or ex smokers | Missing completely at random |
| Diabetes | 10 rows | Majority of the missing occurred are participants receiving inhaler | Missing completely at random |
| Ethnicity | 16 rows | Majority of the missing occurred are participants receiving inhaler | Missing completely at random |

All the variables with missing data are presumed to be missing completely at random because while the majority of the missing data occurred on patients receiving inhaler, there is not enough data to draw a clear pattern.

# Visits data

```{r missing-visits}
colSums(is.na(visits))
kable(table(visits[is.na(visits$walk6min), 'visit']), col.names = c('Visit', 'Total NA'), align = 'l')

invalid_participants = visits[which(visits$visit == 0 & is.na(visits$walk6min)), 'ID']

nrow(visits[visits$ID %in% invalid_participants, ]) # Total rows with missing baseline measures

# Exclude all participants with no baseline measure
valid_visits = visits[!visits$ID %in% invalid_participants, ]
nrow(valid_visits) # 3298 rows left in the visits data
```

Some missing follow-up data is expected and could possibly be because of lost to follow-up. However, missing baseline measure should not happen as it should have been done on enrolment. Moving on with the analysis, participants with missing baseline will be excluded as they may be invalid participants. The total data excluded is only 168 rows or around 1% which would not have a significant impact on the analysis. For the participants without missing baseline but missing follow-up they will still be analysed but only including the valid follow-ups (not NA). Furthermore, attrition grew slightly over the course of the follow-ups with the most lost happening at the fifth follow up at 43 missing, followed with the last follow up at 35 missing. The rest of the follow-ups had mostly around 24 lost to follow-ups. The total data left after excluding this data is 3298 rows.

# Data linkage

Since baseline data has 500 rows of data and visits had 3298 rows of data post data cleaning, after merging there should be 3298 rows of data assuming both datasets contains the same unique participant IDs.

```{r linkage}
linked_data = merge(baseline, valid_visits, by = 'ID',
    all.x = FALSE, all.y = FALSE
)
nrow(linked_data)
```

The total dataset after merging is 3298 rows. **Inner join** is used here because only participants that had their demographic characteristics and exposures taken and had their outcome measures taken are needed for the analysis. Participants that had their demographic characteristics and exposures measured but do not have any baseline or outcome measures (or vice versa, patients that have a baseline or outcome measures but don't exist in the demographic characteristics and exposures dataset) are excluded and treated as invalid participants. The merged dataset now contains the participant information, characteristics such as pre-existing conditions or exposures, as well as their baseline measure and all their follow-ups.

```{r frequency-smoker, tab.cap = 'Total participants for each smoking status'}
total_smokers = as.data.frame(table(baseline$fsmoker))
total_smokers$total_pct = round(total_smokers$Freq / sum(total_smokers$Freq) * 100, 1)
kable(total_smokers, align = 'l',
    col.names = c('Smoking status', 'Total participants (n)', 'Total participants (%)')
)
```

370 of the participants or 74.4% are ex smokers, followed with 87 current smokers or 17.5%, and 4 who never smoked or 8% of the participants.

```{r frequency-phyactivity, tab.cap = 'Total participants for each level of physical activity'}
total_activity = as.data.frame(table(baseline$fphy_activity))
total_activity$total_pct = round(total_activity$Freq / sum(total_activity$Freq) * 100, 1)
kable(total_activity, align = 'l',
    col.names = c('Level of physical activity', 'Total participants (n)', 'Total participants (%)')
)
```

The majority of the participants have low physical activity level with 37%, then high level of physical activity with 29.8%, followed with moderate level of physical activity or 19.1%, and the least frequent is participants who have very high level of physical activity with only 14%.

```{r frequency-smoker-activity, tab.cap = 'Crosstabulation of smoker status and level of physical activity'}
total_smoker_activity = as.data.frame(table(linked_data[, c('fsmoker', 'fphy_activity')]))

pct_within_smoker = round(
    prop.table(
        table(linked_data[, c('fsmoker', 'fphy_activity')]), margin = 1
    ) * 100, 2
) # Fetch the percentage within smokers

pct_within_activity = round(
    prop.table(
        table(linked_data[, c('fsmoker', 'fphy_activity')]), margin = 2
    ) * 100, 2
) # Fetch the percentage within activity level

total_smoker_activity$pct_within_smoker = c(pct_within_smoker)
total_smoker_activity$pct_within_activity = c(pct_within_activity)
kable(total_smoker_activity, align = 'l',
    col.names = c('Smoking status', 'Level of physical activity', 'Total participants')
)
```

```{r distance-per-visit, fig.cap = 'Box plot of distance walked in 6 minutes per visit'}
overall_median = median(linked_data$walk6min, na.rm = TRUE)
ggplot(data = linked_data, aes(x = factor(visit), y = walk6min)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.color = '#D55E00', na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_hline(aes(yintercept = overall_median), 
       linetype = 'solid', linewidth = 0.8,
       colour = '#CC79A7'
    ) +
    labs(
        title = 'Distance walked in 6 minutes per visit',
        x = 'Visit',
        y = 'Distance walked in 6 minutes (m)'
    ) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
    theme_classic()
```

Across all the visits including baseline, the distribution of how far the participants are able to walk in 6 minutes are consistent with a few outliers but not notable. The median and interquartile range of each visit is also similar. The spread of the distance for the baseline and follow-ups are also similar with a few consistent upper outliers. Only two lower outliers exist on the second and sixth follow-up.


```{r distance-for-smoker, warning = FALSE, fig.cap = 'Distance walked in 6 minutes per smoking status'}
overall_mean = mean(linked_data$walk6min, na.rm = TRUE)
ggplot(
      data = linked_data[!is.na(linked_data$fsmoker) & !is.na(linked_data$walk6min), 
      c('walk6min', 'fsmoker')], 
      aes(x = fsmoker, y = walk6min, fill = fsmoker)
    ) +
    geom_violin() +
    geom_jitter(
      alpha = 0.25, size = 0.4, 
      width = 0.08, colour = '#1A1A1A',
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    geom_hline(
      aes(yintercept = overall_mean, linetype ='Overall mean'), 
      linewidth = 0.8, colour = '#444444'
    ) +
    stat_summary(# 1 SD
      fun = mean, 
      fun.min = function(x) mean(x) - sd(x),
      fun.max = function(x) mean(x) + sd(x),
      geom = 'errorbar', colour = '#FFFFFF',
      width = 0.1, linewidth = 0.8,
    ) +
    stat_summary(# Group mean
      fun = mean, geom = 'point',
      colour = '#FFFFFF', size = 2.5,
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(200, 600), breaks = seq(200, 600, 100)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c('#56B4E9', '#009E73', '#CC79A7')) +
    scale_linetype_manual(
      name = '',
      values = c('Overall mean' = 'dashed')
    ) +
    labs(
        title = 'Distance walked in 6 minutes per smoking status',
        x = 'Smoking status',
        y = 'Distance walked in 6 minutes (m)',
        fill = 'Smoking status'
    ) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
      legend.key.width = unit(1, "cm")
    )
```
The mean and one standard deviation spread as denoted by the white error bar within each violin plot, shows that the average of the distance walked in 6 minutes for current smoker is far lower than the participants that have never smoked or ex smokers. Furthermore, the average 6 minutes walk distance of those who never smoked and ex smokers is almost equal and both sits just slightly above the overall average. The shape of the distribution of those who never smoked is slightly left skewed, indicating that there are more participants with higher 6 minutes walk distance. Whereas for ex smoker and current smoker, the distribution is widest below the average, indicating that there are more participants with lower 6 minutes walk distance. However, the maximum outlier or the maximum distance walked in 6 minutes is from the current smoker group, while the minimum is from the ex smoker group.
